judgments.reasoning_cat1: The recitals are narrative and mostly factual, though the assertion that ENET "owns and operates the sole wireless cable system" in the Washington market and the OCR-garbled date and defined term ("SENET") introduce minor imprecision. No operative obligation turns on a single ambiguous word here.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The recital conditions ENET's willingness on "issuance to the University of a license authorizing the University to relocate the D Group Station," while the operative Sections II.D and II.E make denial or conditioned grant merely a termination option; a party could argue the recital states a condition precedent. That gives a modest recital-versus-operative tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A fixed commencement and a fixed expiry date (August 29, 1998) leave nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits consistently with Section I.B's renewal mechanics, which measure the renewal term from the date hereof rather than from the initial term's end; only the interaction, not this clause, is uncertain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The heading says "Automatic Renewal Terms" (plural) but the text grants only "an additional term," and the trailing "unless ENET provides ... ninety days notice" is placed so that its attachment to the whole renewal or only to limb (ii) is arguable. Those are namable textual defects.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections I.C.1 and VIII.B speak of "the automatic renewal term" and "the last automatic renewal term," implying successive renewals that this clause does not provide, and the ten-year outer limit sits awkwardly with III.A's ten-year equipment right. That is a genuine whole-instrument inconsistency about how long the deal runs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "during any or all of the period from the expiration of the automatic renewal term ... through two years thereafter" is opaque as to whether it fixes the lease's commencement window or the window in which offers must arrive, and "material terms and conditions" is itself elastic. The right's temporal reach is genuinely contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with I.C.2's one-year notice and I.C.3's seven/thirty-day mechanics, and with XIII.M's separate exclusive option over channel D2; the "expiration of the automatic renewal term" reference also depends on the plural/singular problem in I.B. A court could find these do not harmonise cleanly.
judgments.clause_name: Section I.C.1 — Right of First Refusal

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The first sentence requires notice "at the commencement of any negotiations," while the last sentence says "[s]uch notice must be given one year prior to expiration of the contract" — two incompatible triggers for the same notice, and "the contract" is undefined (this Agreement or the prospective lease). That is a plain internal ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section I.C.3 adds a seven-day notice on receipt of a bona fide offer, so the instrument contains three different notice deadlines for the same right of first refusal machinery. Reconciling them is not straightforward.
judgments.clause_name: Section I.C.2 — Notice of Negotiations for Lease Commencing Within Two Years

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The mechanics (seven days, thirty days, "substantially the same material terms") are reasonably concrete, though "purpose or the effect of preventing ENET from exercising its Right of First Refusal" is a broad standard. Moderately definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its seven-day trigger sits against I.C.2's requirement of notice one year before expiration and at commencement of negotiations, leaving the sequence of notices uncertain. That interaction is the main exposure.
judgments.clause_name: Section I.C.3 — Notice of Bona Fide Offer; No Offer Preventing Exercise of ROFR

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A straightforward re-trigger rule keyed to a change in "any material term"; "material" is a familiar standard rather than a genuine ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends on the "foregoing subsections," which themselves contain conflicting notice deadlines, but this clause adds no new inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The three applications are specified with reasonable precision, though "such other changes ... as ENET believes necessary" leaves the scope of the STL application to one party's belief. Mild vagueness only.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The reference to a "Leesburg campus" does not match Schedule B, which lists the Northern Virginia campus at Ashburn, a small cross-document mismatch. Otherwise it dovetails with II.A.2 and III.A.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "quality and reliability at least equal to" and "the goals set forth in this paragraph" are workable but soft, and the deemed-agreement-by-filing device could be argued over. Nothing acutely ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The refund of the Commitment Fee here sits beside II.D.1, where the University retains the fee on denial of the Modification Application; the two are triggered by different events but pull in opposite directions on the same money. That is a modest tension.
judgments.clause_name: II.A.2. Design of Facilities and Modification Plan

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "provident," the stray "ECC Applications," and the $15,000 fee-sharing mechanism create small pockets of doubt, but the obligations and the cap are stated concretely. Mostly definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The invitation to the University to share legal fees above $15,000 is hard to square with XIII.N and II.F, under which ENET bears all reasonable costs of the University's applications. That is a real, if narrow, friction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "best efforts," "reasonable requirements of ENET" and an open-ended illustrative list introduced by "including, without limiting the generality" leave the amendment duty's outer boundary uncertain. Namable but familiar softness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is nearly verbatim duplicated by III.E.1 covering modification of built facilities, and the requirement that ENET pre-approve costs in writing cuts against XIII.N's "notwithstanding anything to the contrary" reimbursement promise. Duplication plus that cost tension is worth something.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It calls the instrument "this Service Agreement" and lower-cases "commitment fee" while cross-referring to a definition, and cites "Paragraph XII.A" for the best-efforts duty that actually appears in II.B. Those are mechanical slips affecting the reference points.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Retention of the Commitment Fee here contrasts with II.A.2's refund on failed negotiations, and the mis-citation to XII.A rather than II.B must be harmonised. Moderate relational doubt.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "alternative transmission source" and "cannot be utilized by ENET" are undefined and judged by no stated standard, and the ten-day clock starts from an event (inability to use an alternative) that is not itself datable. That is a genuine vagueness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Like II.D.1 it cross-refers to Paragraph XII.A for best efforts that are in II.B, and the excusal of STL/PTP obligations must be read against III.A and III.D. Modest.
judgments.clause_name: II.D.2. Denial of STL or PTP Application

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "conditions materially adverse to ENET" is the operative trigger and is a matter of degree with no benchmark. That is a namable vague term, though a common one.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coordinates sensibly with II.E.2 and II.E.3 and with the XI termination scheme; the only wrinkle is the same XII.A cross-reference slip. Low.
judgments.clause_name: II.E.1. Grant of Modification Application with Conditions

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Again "materially adverse" governs, and the rescission device gives the University power to reverse ENET's termination, which reads oddly but is stated clearly. Moderate vagueness only.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is symmetrical with II.D.2's excusal mechanism and consistent with III.A's excusal of STL/PTP work; no conflict identified.
judgments.clause_name: II.E.2. Grant of STL or PTP Application with Conditions

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause does not say what happens if the University rejects ENET's indemnification offer, or whether ENET's offer suspends the termination, and "reasonable discretion" over acceptance compounds it. That gap is a real construction point.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps with IX.B/IX.A indemnity machinery and with XI.C's preservation of damages, but nothing squarely contradicts it.
judgments.clause_name: II.E.3. Conditions Adverse to the University

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "All reasonable costs and expenses, including legal and engineering" is broad but the allocation is unqualified and clear on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: XIII.N caps reimbursement of negotiation legal and engineering fees at $15,000, and II.B/XIII.A invite the University to share fees above $15,000, whereas this clause puts all reasonable preparation costs on ENET without limit. That is a specific conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "state-of-the-art equipment," "appropriate space," "then-current market value" and the typo "from the date hereon" all invite argument, and the $1.00 purchase right turns on classification of equipment "shared with other stations." Several namable soft terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It excepts nonrenewal caused by "the exercise by ENET of its rights under Section XI.B.(2)," but XI.B(2) is a termination-for-breach right, not a nonrenewal right, and the ten-year equipment right must be squared with I.B's renewal limit. That cross-reference mismatch is a genuine relational problem.
judgments.clause_name: III.A. Construction of Modified D Group Station, STL Link and PTP Link

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It obliges ENET to reorient the antennas at receive sites "listed on Schedule A," but Schedule A is the programming list; the intended reference is plainly Schedule B. That is a mechanical error going to the scope of the obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section X.B.5 confirms Schedule B identifies the receive sites, so this clause's citation contradicts the schedule structure, and Schedule B itself contains "Omitted" entries. The mis-reference is a concrete inconsistency with the rest of the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The final phrase "begun broadcasting the D Group" is incomplete (the D Group what?), and the Start Date depends on completing all three facilities plus the Modification Plan, so a partial excusal under II.D.2 leaves the trigger unclear. That is a namable defect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section V.C keys the first royalty to the D Group Station being "constructed and ... broadcasting at ENET's wireless cable headend," a different formula from the Start Date, and III.B's antenna work is due "[p]rior to the Start Date" though it forms part of the Modification Plan. Those mismatched triggers are a real relational point.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The division of responsibility is spelled out with a helpful parenthetical example, and the exception for "intentional actions or gross negligence of the University" is stated. Fairly definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits IV's definition of University Capacity and XIII.N's reimbursement of operating costs, though the latter's "notwithstanding anything to the contrary" language duplicates cost allocation. No real conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Same soft standards as II.C.1 — "best efforts," "reasonable requirements," open-ended "including" list — with the added contingency of ENET's advance written cost approval. Moderate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It substantially duplicates II.C.1, and its pre-approval condition sits against XIII.N's unqualified reimbursement obligation; IV also ties allocation consequences to this paragraph. Modest incoherence risk.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The commencement trigger is a compound of unverifiable market facts ("reliable and cost-effective" equipment "available for immediate purchase") and the obligation is qualified by "if possible consistent with the FCC's then-existing rules." Those conditions are hard to apply.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It directs compression onto "channel D1," yet Section IV allocates D3 and D4 to ENET and ties digital-technology consequences to recapture on D3 and D4, and D2 is Hybrid's; the channel reference looks inconsistent with the allocation scheme. That is a specific mismatch.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear prohibition qualified by consent "not [to] be unreasonably withheld"; the standard is familiar and the subject matter definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It restrains the University from relocating the station, while VIII.B lets the University surrender or not renew the licence altogether and III.E.1 obliges it to apply for relocation at ENET's request; the boundary is arguable but the clauses can be harmonised. Modest.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The University grants "the entire 6 MHz transmission capacity" of D3 and D4 yet reserves a right to "recapture ... simultaneous use" of the same channels, and the defined term is mistyped as "SENET Capacity"; the reduction-on-digital sentence is also convoluted. Those are namable defects.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cross-refers to Paragraphs III.E.1 and III.E.2, but III.E.2 addresses compression on channel D1 while this clause adjusts recapture on D3 and D4, and XIII.M's D2 option and XIII.Q's Hybrid subordination further complicate the allocation. Genuine whole-instrument friction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single fixed sum payable on execution; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its fate on early termination is addressed in II.A.2 (refund less costs) and II.D.1 (retention), which cut different ways but by reference to different events. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The enumeration is broken — "the greater of: Two Thousand Five Hundred Dollars ($2,500.00) or (ii) Twenty Cents ($0.20)" omits "(i)" — and it does not say the per-subscriber figure is a monthly rate, leaving the comparison arguable. That is a mechanical error touching the core payment term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with V.B.1's subscriber count, V.C's payment dates, V.F's proration against the $2,500 floor, and XIII.M's additional royalty on the same greater-of formula; the floor and proration interact imperfectly. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The bulk-billing formula says the revenues are "determined by dividing the total monthly revenues ... in said bulk billing divided by" the prevailing rate — a duplicated verb — and "isolated locations in the same facility" is internally odd. Mechanical defects, though the arithmetic is guessable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It elaborates V.B without contradicting V.C's certificate requirement or V.D's audit right.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The certificate must show subscribers "served during each month of such period," but no "period" has been defined, and the count under V.B.1 is a first-of-month snapshot rather than a monthly average. That mismatch is namable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its trigger — station "constructed and ... broadcasting at ENET's wireless cable headend" — differs from the Start Date defined in III.C, so the date the first royalty falls due is contestable. That is a specific inconsistency.
judgments.clause_name: V.C. Required Certificate and Payment Dates

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The eighteen-month retention period sits against an audit window extending to ninety days after service ends, and "at any time or times" jars with the once-per-calendar-year limit and thirty-business-day notice. Some internal friction but the mechanics are workable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing elsewhere in the Agreement contradicts the audit right; V.B.1 supplies the figures to be audited.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear non-interference covenant with a clear consequence; "lawfully" is the only qualifier and is unremarkable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the royalty being subscriber-count based rather than revenue-share based under V.B.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[P]roportionately reduced" is clear arithmetic in principle, but it is silent on whether the $2,500 minimum in V.B is itself prorated or applies in full. That gap is namable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with V.B's greater-of floor and XIII.M's additional royalty; the floor question is the same one, so the tension is mild rather than a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "gross charge" is used without definition and the carve-out is only for "taxes on the income of ENET," so which "fees" fall on the University is arguable. A namable but narrow ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It does not collide with XIII.N or II.F, which address reimbursement of the University's costs rather than taxes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The obligation is measured by what is "customarily insured against by firms of established reputations" in "such amounts as are customarily carried," then extended by "including, without limitation" over two enumerated policies — a classic general-versus-specific scope question. That is exactly the tension the category describes.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: VI.A.1, VI.A.2 and VI.B carry it through coherently; no other provision contradicts the insurance duty.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "All-risk" at 100% of full replacement value without depreciation deduction is a definite, quantified requirement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with VI.A's introduction and VI.B's policy-form requirements.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The limits are stated numerically and by category; the only flaw is a missing final period. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits the insurance section and IX.A's indemnity without conflict.
judgments.clause_name: VI.A.2. Comprehensive General Public Liability Insurance

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "as appropriate, designate the University as either the insured party or as an additional insured" leaves the choice and its trigger unstated, which is a namable soft spot. The notice and delivery duties are otherwise concrete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coheres with VI.A and with III.A's allocation of equipment ownership; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A list of permitted categories closes with "or an other programming agreed to by the University" — a garbled catch-all against enumerated specifics — and the clause both requires consent "not [to] be unreasonably withheld" and reserves an "absolute right to deny" obscene programming. Both a mechanical slip and a general-versus-specific tension are present.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It treats Schedule A as "identif[ying]" permitted networks, but Schedule A is headed "REPRESENTATIVE PROGRAMMING SERVICE" and lists only representative types, so the permitted scope is uncertain; IV's grant of use "for any legal purpose" also pulls against this consent regime. That is a concrete inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "required or desired" and "best efforts to take all actions reasonably required" are elastic, and "all necessary steps to renew" is absolute in the same breath. Moderate vagueness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The "[e]xcept as set forth in Section VIII.B" carve-out largely reconciles it with the University's right to surrender or not renew, though the two remain in tension with XIII.G's no-adverse-action covenant. Modest.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It permits surrender "at anytime within two years after the expiration of the last automatic renewal term," a period when the Agreement has ended, so the source of the continuing obligation is unclear; "assumeall remaining obligations" is also run together. Namable defects.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates much of XIII.A's assignment machinery while XIII.A separately allows assignment to a non-assuming entity, and "last automatic renewal term" presupposes plural renewals that I.B does not clearly give. Real relational friction.
judgments.clause_name: VIII.B. Return or Nonrenewal of License

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The second limb sweeps in "any other claimed harm or unlawfulness arising from the transmission of any programming" after specific libel, slander and IP claims — a catch-all against enumerated specifics — while limb (iii) is confined to gross negligence. That contrast invites argument about scope.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coheres with VII's obscenity controls and IX.C's claims procedure; the University's own control over programming under VII could be argued to cut down the indemnity, but no direct conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A mirror-image indemnity with the same three enumerated triggers and no open-ended tail; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with IX.A and IX.C.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The procedure is sequenced and conditional, with "in form and substance satisfactory to the Claiming Party" as the only soft term. Largely definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It applies to both IX.A and IX.B without contradiction; II.E.3's ad hoc indemnity offer is outside this section but not inconsistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard organisation representation with a forward-looking covenant; nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with X.C's survival provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Broad but conventional compliance and no-conflict language; "all laws, rules and regulations governing its business and the ITFS facilities" is wide yet not genuinely ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits X.C and the FCC-related covenants in VIII and XII.
judgments.clause_name: X.A.2. Compliance with Agreements and Law (ENET)

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence authority representation with no elastic term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the rest of Section X.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Knowledge qualifiers ("to its best knowledge") are conventional and the categories are enumerated; definite enough.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No conflict with any other provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "reasonable assurance of the funding necessary" states no standard, source or amount, so whether the representation is met is almost unadjudicable. That is a namable vagueness in a single short sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It bears on ENET's extensive cost obligations (II.F, XIII.N) but nothing contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Organisation, power and FCC eligibility stated plainly with a continuing covenant.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with VIII.A's licence-maintenance duties.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard compliance and no-conflict representation, qualified "in all material respects"; nothing genuinely ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It warrants that performance will not conflict with "any agreement or commitment to which it is bound," yet XIII.Q expressly contemplates "conflicts between the two agreements" with Hybrid and subordinates ENET's rights accordingly. That is a specific tension.
judgments.clause_name: X.B.2. Compliance with Agreements and Law (University)

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, definite authority representation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the rest of Section X.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Mirrors X.A.4 with an added materiality qualifier; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No conflict identified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A flat accuracy warranty about a schedule; the only softness is what "the site and receive antenna" must include.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Schedule B as annexed contains several entries marked "Omitted" and incomplete coordinates, and III.B mistakenly refers receive sites to Schedule A, so the warranty is hard to square with the documents attached. That is a concrete mismatch.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Survival and continuing-notification duties stated clearly; "might reasonably be deemed to constitute" is soft but marginal.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections X.A and X.B and with the termination scheme in XI.
judgments.clause_name: X.C. Survival of Representations and Warranties

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The structure "either (a) ENET has not cured such breach within thirty (30) days, or (b) ... has not undertaken material or substantive measures to cure" makes the two limbs alternative rather than cumulative, so limb (b) adds nothing and the cure right is unclear; "material or substantive measures" is also unmeasured. Genuine textual defect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: XI.B(2) uses the same limbs but joins them differently, and III.A attaches a $1.00 equipment purchase right to termination under this paragraph, raising the stakes of the ambiguity. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limb (1) lets ENET terminate on FCC revocation "unless such termination is due to a breach by ENET," and limb (3) lets ENET terminate simply because it "ceases to provide wireless cable service" — a self-triggered exit that is clear but strikingly one-sided. The cure structure repeats XI.A's ambiguity in different words.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: III.A cross-refers to "Section XI.B.(2)" as a ground of nonrenewal though it is a termination ground, and limb (3) allows ENET to escape the whole bargain, which sits uneasily with I.B's renewal expectations and the University's ROFR scheme. That is a real coherence question.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and clear on its face: termination does not bar the terminating party's damages claim; it is silent on the non-terminating party's claims.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections XI.A and XI.B say termination is "without further liability" to the other party, and II.D/II.E terminations are "without further liability between the parties," so this clause's preservation of damages must be reconciled with those phrases. That is a specific, arguable conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The first sentence makes filings "subject to the approval of the University, which approval shall not be unreasonably withheld," while the second, "[n]otwithstanding anything herein to the contrary," makes the University's advance consent an unqualified precondition — the two sentences pull against each other. That is a namable internal inconsistency.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section II.A.2 obliges the University either to file within thirty days or to negotiate revisions, which fits the reasonableness limb but not the unqualified-consent limb, and several clauses cite XII.A as the source of the parties' best-efforts prosecution duty that actually sits in II.B. Real relational friction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It uses "best reasonable efforts" and "reasonable best efforts" in successive sentences and imposes an open-ended duty to cooperate with "all reasonable requests" for "any additional facilities." The efforts standards are muddled.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It speaks of optimising ENET's business "within the Washington/Baltimore area" whereas the recitals and XI.B(3) use the Washington, DC metropolitan area, and the duty to obtain licences overlaps VIII.A. Modest inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The doubled "incurred by the University" is a slip but the allocation is clear and limited to Section XII obligations.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps II.F and XIII.N, and XIII.N's $15,000 cap on negotiation fees plus II.B's fee-sharing invitation make the overall reimbursement scheme untidy. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The second sentence begins "Subject to the foregoing provisions" yet permits precisely what the first sentence forbids — assignment to an entity that does not assume the Agreement — which is self-contradictory as drafted. That is a plain intrinsic defect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It also duplicates VIII.B's surrender/assignment machinery and, unlike II.B, makes ENET's $15,000 notice mandatory ("shall notify") rather than permissive, so the fee-sharing regimes differ. Genuine incoherence with the rest.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate counterparts clause with no elastic term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the execution block and XIII.D.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "ENET shall assist in the development of such program" states an obligation with no content, scope or cost allocation, and "sufficiently in advance" is unmeasured. The assistance duty is genuinely vague.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coheres with IV's University Capacity and III.D's transmission duty; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard merger and written-modification clause; "with respect to the subject matter" is the only soft edge.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Agreement repeatedly incorporates the separate Hybrid Agreement's constraints (III.E.1, XIII.Q) and the Modification Plan, which a party might argue sits awkwardly with an entire-agreement statement, though Hybrid is a different counterparty. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare acknowledgment of executory character with no operative content to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing in the Agreement contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The enumerated events close with "or other contingencies beyond the reasonable control of the parties" — a catch-all against a specific list — and "the period of dependency of any such contingency" is apparently a mis-transcription of "pendency." Both a scope tension and a mechanical slip.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its automatic extension of time-limited duties runs against XIII.R's time-of-the-essence clause and the tight ten-day windows in II.D and II.E, though the "[n]otwithstanding anything ... to the contrary" opener gives it priority. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[W]ill not take any action which would adversely affect the rights granted" is an unbounded negative covenant with no materiality or good-faith limit. That breadth is namable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: VIII.B expressly permits the University to surrender or not renew its licence on a year's notice, which would plainly affect ENET's rights, and III.E.3/XIII.Q also carve out permitted adverse acts. That is a real tension with an enumerated right.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Choice of the Communications Act, FCC Rules and DC law is stated definitely, though it does not rank federal and local sources if they diverge. Minor.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with XIII.K's venue clause and the FCC-centred obligations throughout.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard headings disclaimer; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It arguably neutralises reliance on the "Automatic Renewal Terms" heading in I.B, which is a use rather than a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear waiver of contra proferentem with no ambiguous term of its own.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the whole; it bears on how other ambiguities are resolved rather than creating one.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[A]ny party shall have the right to sue the other party in District of Columbia courts" is permissive while the following sentence is an irrevocable submission and venue waiver, leaving exclusivity uncertain. That is a namable ambiguity, if a familiar one.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coheres with XIII.H's governing law and XIII.L's notice provision for service; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Delivery methods, deeming rule and addresses are specified; "Except as set forth above concerning the payment of Royalties" is a clear carve-out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: V.C permits royalty payment by first class mail, which this clause expressly excepts, so the two fit; XIII.K relies on this clause for service. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "ENET shall have the exclusive tight to lease the capacity of channel D2 for the duration of this Agreement" states a right whose relationship to the twenty-one-day option mechanic is unclear, and the additional royalty repeats the greater-of formula. Moderate ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: XIII.Q subordinates all ENET rights to the Hybrid Agreement "notwithstanding anything to the contrary," and IV defines ENET Capacity as D3 and D4 only, so an exclusive D2 right needs reconciling with both. That is a specific relational conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It opens "[n]otwithstanding anything to the contrary contained herein" and promises reimbursement of "all reasonable costs and expenses," then caps negotiation legal and engineering fees at $15,000 — the interaction of the override and the cap is arguable. Namable tension.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: II.F puts all reasonable preparation costs on ENET without cap, II.B and XIII.A invite the University to share fees above $15,000, and II.C.1/III.E.1 condition cost-bearing on ENET's advance written approval; this override cannot easily be harmonised with all of them. Real conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The disclaimer of joint venture and of holding out is stated plainly, subject to the terms of the Agreement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with III.D's supervision arrangement and VII's programming controls; no conflict identified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[A]dversely affect the ability of the parties to perform" and "as nearly as reasonably possible" are soft, and the duty is only to negotiate in good faith with no fallback if negotiation fails. Moderate vagueness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coheres with XIII.P.2's acknowledgment of future FCC rule changes and with the II.D/II.E termination options; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare acknowledgment with no operative obligation; it is definite in substance.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cites the Report and Order as released July 9, 1994 while Section IV cites the same order as released July 6, 1994, and the acknowledgment that allocation is subject to change sits against IV's fixed D3/D4 allocation. Modest inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It says the University's obligations "shall be read to conform" to its Hybrid obligations and bars any action having "an adverse effect on the rights of Hybrid" as judged by the University's "reasonable judgment" — a broad, self-assessed override. That breadth is a namable weakness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: XIII.M gives ENET an exclusive right to lease channel D2, X.B.2 warrants no conflict with other agreements, and III.A obliges ENET to give Hybrid access; this "notwithstanding anything to the contrary" subordination cuts across those. A specific conflict exists.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line time-of-the-essence clause, definite on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It applies to a document full of "as soon as reasonably possible," "best efforts" and open-ended standards, and XIII.F automatically extends time-limited duties on force majeure; those are hard to reconcile with strict time being essential. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional non-waiver clause; "express or implied waiver" is the only curiosity and it is standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the cure and termination machinery in XI.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The "Final Order" definition is carefully structured in two limbs; "variations therefore" is a slip for "therefrom" that does not change meaning. Largely definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: II.D.1 refers to the definition as being in "Paragraph XIII.T," which matches, and the definition is used consistently across II.D, II.E, VIII.B and XIII.A.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It describes the list only as "representative types" of programming ENET "intends" to transmit, which is not the language of a definitive permitted-content schedule, and it cross-refers to "Subparagraph 3 (C)," a provision that does not exist in this Agreement. Both a vagueness and a mechanical cross-reference error.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section VII treats Schedule A as "identif[ying]" the networks ENET may transmit and Section III.B mistakenly refers receive sites to Schedule A, so the schedule's function cannot be reconciled with the operative text. That is a concrete inconsistency.
